intro_title: AI gets cheaper to use—and harder to supervise
intro: Today’s issue follows AI into everyday chat, weather warnings, biological design, business operations and personal decisions. Wider access is arriving alongside a practical warning: capable agents still need stronger boundaries than a stream of approval buttons.
friendly_intro_title: AI is easier to use, but still needs careful rules
friendly_intro: Today we look at cheaper and more useful AI for chat, weather, science, work and dating. We also explain why clicking “allow” is not enough to keep AI agents safe.

items.title: ChatGPT gives free users unlimited GPT-5.6 Luna text chats
items.summary: OpenAI is making GPT-5.6 Luna the default for Free and Go users, with unlimited text chats and a Think button for harder questions. Plus and Pro users get a more focused GPT-5.6 Sol and a slider for controlling reasoning effort.
items.why_it_matters: The useful baseline for free AI rises sharply: long-running text help becomes easier to access without watching a message counter. Tool use, files and images still have limits, so “unlimited” applies specifically to text chats.
items.friendly_title: Free ChatGPT users get unlimited text chats
items.friendly_summary: OpenAI is giving free users unlimited text chats with GPT-5.6 Luna. Paid users also get better answer controls.
items.friendly_why: You can use ChatGPT for longer writing, learning and planning sessions without running out of text messages. Files and images still have limits.

items.title: WeatherNext adds about a day of accuracy to cyclone forecasts
items.summary: Google DeepMind says WeatherNext predicts cyclone tracks, intensity and wind structure with a lead-time advantage of more than 24 hours over earlier leading systems. The Nature-published work has already supported operational forecasts, and the models are being open-sourced.
items.why_it_matters: An extra day of useful warning can improve evacuation, logistics and emergency planning. Open weights also give weather agencies and researchers a path to test and adapt the system rather than relying only on a closed forecast feed.
items.friendly_title: AI cyclone forecasts may give people one more day to prepare
items.friendly_summary: Google’s WeatherNext model can predict where cyclones go and how strong they become about one day earlier than older leading systems.
items.friendly_why: Earlier warnings can help families, emergency teams and businesses prepare. Google is also sharing the models for researchers to test.

items.title: Evo 2 designs whole phage genomes that kill E. coli
items.summary: Stanford researchers used the Evo 2 genome model to design nearly 300 bacteriophages, then found 16 strong E. coli killers in laboratory tests. A cocktail of the generated phages also overcame bacteria resistant to the original natural phage.
items.why_it_matters: This is a concrete laboratory result, not just a computer prediction, and it points toward new ways to tackle antibiotic resistance. It also raises the stakes for biosecurity controls around models that can write functional genomes.
items.friendly_title: AI designed viruses that killed harmful bacteria in the lab
items.friendly_summary: Stanford scientists used AI to design tiny viruses called phages. Sixteen of them were very good at killing E. coli bacteria in tests.
items.friendly_why: This could help create new treatments when antibiotics stop working. It also shows why powerful biology AI needs strong safety checks.

items.title: Qwen3.8 Max pairs a one-million-token context with mid-tier pricing
items.summary: Independent testing from Artificial Analysis gives Qwen3.8 Max an Intelligence Index score of 58, with image and video input, a one-million-token context window and API pricing of $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens. The model ranked strongly on intelligence but was relatively verbose and slightly slower than the comparison median.
items.why_it_matters: The model is a credible option for large-document and multimodal workflows, but its high output volume can increase real task costs. Teams should compare cost per completed job, not just the attractive headline token price.
items.friendly_title: Qwen3.8 Max handles very large files at a reasonable price
items.friendly_summary: Independent tests show Qwen3.8 Max is a strong model with a very large memory window. It can read text, images and video, but it often writes long answers.
items.friendly_why: It may suit big research or document tasks. Check the total cost of its long answers before using it at scale.

items.title: Human reviewers missed one in three risky agent commands
items.summary: Across more than 40,000 runs of a browser-based agent-permission game, players missed one in three threats on average. Familiar-looking npm scripts were a particular blind spot, and only about one in five players caught every threat without heavily blocking safe commands.
items.why_it_matters: Approval prompts are not a complete security boundary: repetition, time pressure and missing context wear reviewers down. Run agents inside narrow sandboxes, limit secrets and permissions, and reserve human approval for clear high-risk transitions.
items.friendly_title: People missed many dangerous AI agent requests
items.friendly_summary: In a game with more than 40,000 runs, people allowed about one in three dangerous commands. Normal-looking software commands were easy to trust by mistake.
items.friendly_why: Do not depend only on “allow” buttons. Give AI agents limited access and keep private keys and important files outside their workspace.

items.title: Anthropic starts building a custom AI chip design team
items.summary: Anthropic confirmed that it is assembling a custom-silicon team to co-design AI hardware and models for better speed and efficiency. The move complements its existing compute agreements with AWS, Google, Nvidia and AMD rather than replacing them immediately.
items.why_it_matters: Model competition is moving down into chips, where efficiency gains can affect API prices, availability and latency. Customers should expect providers to differentiate increasingly on the full hardware-and-model stack.
items.friendly_title: Anthropic wants to design chips for Claude
items.friendly_summary: Anthropic is hiring engineers to help design special AI chips. It wants Claude to run faster and more efficiently.
items.friendly_why: Better chips may eventually make AI services faster, cheaper and easier to scale.

items.title: Google reshapes DeepMind leadership around research and products
items.summary: Demis Hassabis is moving from Google DeepMind CEO to Alphabet chief scientist and DeepMind chairman, while Koray Kavukcuoglu takes day-to-day control. Reuters also reports several prominent engineers, including Jeff Dean, are leaving to form a machine-learning research startup.
items.why_it_matters: Leadership changes can alter how quickly Gemini research becomes dependable products and cloud services. Businesses building on Google’s AI stack should watch product roadmaps and staffing continuity, not just benchmark announcements.
items.friendly_title: Google changes who leads its AI work
items.friendly_summary: Demis Hassabis will focus more on science, while another leader runs DeepMind’s daily work. Several well-known engineers are also leaving Google.
items.friendly_why: These changes may affect how quickly new Gemini tools arrive and how strongly Google focuses on business products.

items.title: Naïve packages company operations behind one agent-ready API
items.summary: Naïve has raised $28.5 million for infrastructure that lets developers connect agents to payments, email, phone numbers, cloud services, storage and company incorporation through one API. The company says it signed up more than 30,000 developer customers within months.
items.why_it_matters: Agent tooling is moving beyond generating code into operating a business. That can remove setup work for small teams, but financial and legal actions require explicit spending limits, audit logs and human accountability.
items.friendly_title: A new service helps AI agents run business tasks
items.friendly_summary: Naïve gives AI agents one way to use payments, email, phone numbers, cloud tools and company setup services.
items.friendly_why: Small teams could save time on boring setup work. Money and legal actions still need clear limits and careful review.

items.title: Dating apps test AI matchmaking instead of endless swiping
items.summary: A new group of dating apps, including Ditto, is replacing large swipe queues with AI-led introductions based on conversations and stated preferences. The approach promises fewer, more deliberate matches, while asking users to share unusually personal data with an algorithm.
items.why_it_matters: AI is starting to mediate intimate choices, not just office tasks. Anyone trying these services should examine how conversation data is stored, whether profiles can be deleted and how much control the system has over introductions.
items.friendly_title: Some dating apps now use AI instead of swiping
items.friendly_summary: New dating apps talk with users and use AI to suggest a smaller number of possible matches.
items.friendly_why: This may save time, but it requires sharing personal information. Check the app’s privacy and deletion rules first.

items.title: Microsoft opens its largest India data-centre hub
items.summary: Microsoft has opened its largest Indian data centre in Hyderabad, creating its fourth cloud region in the country, with Adani Group and HDFC Bank among early users. The facility is part of a roughly $20.5 billion expansion commitment in India.
items.why_it_matters: Local infrastructure can reduce latency and help organisations keep regulated data closer to home, widening practical access to cloud AI. The scale of investment also makes energy, water and grid planning part of the real cost of AI adoption.
items.friendly_title: Microsoft opens a large new AI data centre in India
items.friendly_summary: Microsoft has opened its biggest data-centre site in India. It will support cloud and AI services for local businesses.
items.friendly_why: Nearby servers can make services faster and help with local data rules. Large sites also use a lot of power and water.

items.title: AionUi puts multiple coding agents in one always-on workspace
items.summary: AionUi is an open-source desktop workspace for running and coordinating more than 20 command-line agents, including Hermes, Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode. It has about 31,600 GitHub stars and was among the day’s strongest AI-related trending repositories.
items.how_its_useful: Use it when you want one interface for several local agent tools, scheduled work and team-style delegation. Review each agent’s permissions before enabling always-on operation, especially around repositories and credentials.
items.friendly_title: AionUi brings many coding agents into one app
items.friendly_summary: AionUi is a free desktop app that can run Hermes, Claude Code, Codex and many other AI agents together.
items.friendly_useful: It can reduce tool switching and help organise several agents. Limit what each agent can access before leaving it running.

items.title: AutoGPT remains a heavily used platform for building agent workflows
items.summary: AutoGPT is an open-source platform for creating, deploying and managing continuous AI agents and workflow blocks. With roughly 186,000 stars, it returned to GitHub’s daily Python trending list while continuing active development.
items.how_its_useful: Use AutoGPT to prototype multi-step automations and assemble reusable agent workflows rather than writing every integration from scratch. Start with low-risk data and strict budgets because continuous agents can consume tokens and trigger external actions quickly.
items.friendly_title: AutoGPT helps people build multi-step AI workers
items.friendly_summary: AutoGPT is a popular open-source system for building AI agents that follow workflows and keep working across several steps.
items.friendly_useful: It is useful for testing repeatable automations. Set spending and access limits before letting an agent run for a long time.

items.title: Scientific Agent Skills gives coding agents 158 research workflows
items.summary: Scientific Agent Skills is a library of 158 reusable workflows and connections to more than 100 scientific databases for biology, chemistry, medicine and drug discovery. The repository has about 32,800 stars and added more than 100 stars on the day’s Python trending list.
items.how_its_useful: Researchers can add structured literature, database and analysis procedures to compatible agents such as Codex, Claude Code and Cursor. Treat outputs as research assistance, verify citations and keep clinical or experimental decisions with qualified humans.
items.friendly_title: Scientific Agent Skills adds research tools to AI agents
items.friendly_summary: This free library gives AI coding agents ready-made steps for science tasks and access to many research databases.
items.friendly_useful: It can speed up literature and data work. Always check sources and let trained experts make medical or laboratory decisions.
